British Values
The DfE have reinforced the need to “create and enforce a clear and rigorous expectation on all schools to promote the fundamental British values of democracy, the rule of law, individual liberty, mutual respect and tolerance of those with different faiths and beliefs.” The government set out its definition of British values in the 2011 Prevent Strategy, and these values have been reiterated in 2014.
At Tottenhall these values are reinforced regularly and in the following ways:
DEMOCRACY
THE RULE OF LAW
Rules are consistently reinforced at Tottenhall
INDIVIDUAL LIBERTY
As Tottenhall pupils are actively encouraged to make choices, knowing that they are in a safe and supportive environment. As a school we educate and provide boundaries for your pupils to make informed choices, through a safe environment and an empowering curriculum.
MUTUAL RESPECT
Mutual respect is at the heart of Tottenhall ethos and values. Pupils learn that their behaviours have an effect on their own rights and those of others. All members of the school community treat each other with respect.
Ethos and Values we promote through our Golden Rules:
Be gentle
Be kind and helpful
Work hard
Look after property
Keep yourself and others safe
TOLERANCE OF THOSE OF DIFFERENT FAITHS AND BELIEFS
Tottenhall is a richly diverse school. We actively promote diversity through our celebrations of different faiths and cultures. Religious educations and PHSE lessons reinforce message of tolerance and respect for others. Members of different faiths and religions are encouraged to share their knowledge to enhance learning within classes and the school. Our school curriculum consistently encourages educational visits to different places of worship. Last year the pupils visited a Mosque, Synagogue and Christian Church.

pageCache.text:
Vision, Aims and Values
Our Vision
We believe in creating lifelong learners in a safe stimulating environment where children are nurtured and inspired to be the best they can be.
We want all our pupils to recognise the value they bring by just being themselves as well as growing their minds to achieve better outcomes throughout their lives. They are encouraged to capitalise on their strengths and to have the courage and confidence to face new challenges through fun, interactive learning experiences. We have the highest expectations for all our pupils regardless of their abilities and needs. We work in partnership with parents, governors and the wider school community to inform our decision making. Our relationships are built on trust, mutual respect, sharing of information and a willingness to learn from each other.
Our Aims
The staff and the governors work together:
Pupils enjoy the activities they do in lessons. This encourages good behaviour and little interruption to their concentration.
Ofsted Report – 2021
Our Values
Conny ConfidenceConfident children are not afraid to make mistakes when learning something new
Oscar OrganisationChildren who are organised plan to do their best work. They listen carefully to what their teachers and parents want them to do
Pete PersistenceChildren who are persistent keep on trying when things seem hard or are not fun to do
Ricky ResilienceChildren who are emotionally resilient can calm down soon after being extremely upset without needing the immediate help of an adult
Gabby Get AlongGetting along means that children work and play together nicely. It means that children tell the truth, care about and are friendly to others.

Headteacher's Welcome
On behalf of myself, the staff, governors and pupils, I would like to welcome you to Tottenhall Infant School.
At Tottenhall Infant School, we value each child as an individual and support them to develop their unique abilities and ambitions. We are determined for all pupils to become resilient independent learners, equipped with the skills to achieve their full potential. Children have a happy, successful journey full of enjoyment and eagerness to learn and achieve well. We are committed to providing the best start in education for all our children in a caring, inclusive and nurturing environment. Throughout our curriculum we aim to challenge and motivate pupils and enable them to participate in a range of high-quality learning opportunities. All our staff and governors work incredibly hard to ensure our children receive an excellent education to ‘be the best they can be.’
To support our mission, we have a set of shared values for all members of our community to embrace. The 5 values of resilience, confidence, persistence, getting along and organisation are embedded throughout our school and are reflected in children’s achievements and individual personalities.
Leaders, governors and staff make sure that safeguarding is robust and protects pupils, staff, visitors and the wider community. Keeping our pupils safe ensures they will be ready to engage in learning across all aspects of school life.
As parents and carers, you are the most important people in our pupil’s lives. We encourage your involvement in school life and value your comments and suggestions on improving the opportunities we provide. Please take some time to browse the website to see what we have to offer our children. We strongly recommend visits in person to the school to get a feel for our ethos and environment.
School tours for prospective parents take place on Tuesday mornings when the headteacher is available to conduct a tour. Please contact the school office to arrange an appointment.
Mrs Zaheen Younis Headteacher

Religious Education
At Tottenhall Infant School, Religious Education (RE) invites children to explore life’s big questions, discovering what people believe, how those beliefs shape the way they live, and how this helps us make sense of our own ideas and ways of living.
We follow the Enfield Agreed Syllabus for Religious Education, developed by the Enfield SACRE (Standing Advisory Council on Religious Education) and updated in September 2023. This syllabus is built around three key strands — Believing, Expressing, and Living — which are revisited each year through carefully planned units of learning. Each unit focuses on a ‘big question’ designed to deepen understanding, build knowledge progressively, and develop children’s skills of reflection and enquiry.
RE at Tottenhall encourages pupils to think deeply about meaning, purpose, belief, right and wrong, and what it means to be human. It nurtures awareness, knowledge and understanding of a wide range of world faiths, religious traditions, and world views.
Through this learning, pupils develop a sense of identity and belonging. RE helps them to grow as individuals and as members of both their local and global communities, fostering respect, empathy and understanding for people of all faiths and none. It is an essential part of a broad and balanced curriculum that prepares our pupils for life in a diverse society.
We believe that RE learning extends beyond the classroom. Trips and visits to places of worship, visits from faith leaders, and immersive RE experiences all enrich our curriculum, helping to bring stories, traditions and beliefs to life in memorable and meaningful ways.
“RE and a deeper appreciation of faith and belief can play an important part in supporting our borough’s tradition of respect and co-operation within and between its different communities… The insights and personal foundations that can be acquired through studying the world’s great faith traditions and belief systems have never been more important or relevant.”
London Borough of Enfield, SACRE 2023

Science
At Tottenhall, we provide a high-quality Science education that focuses on introducing our young learners to the world around them through hands-on exploration and engaging activities. They are encouraged to be curious, ask questions, and are supported in developing their understanding of scientific ideas to answer their own questions. Pupils are offered opportunities and experiences to observe and understand the wonders of their surroundings, promoting a fascination and a lifelong love for Science. We aim for pupils to leave Tottenhall with a secure understanding of scientific concepts and a passion for scientific enquiry by delivering a broad, balanced, and coherent curriculum which embeds both scientific skills and knowledge. By doing this, we not only seek to continually ignite our pupils’ curiosity and interests but also prepare them to be inquisitive, confident, and skilful scientists!
We use the National Curriculum to ensure comprehensive coverage of learning, with long, medium, and short-term plans carefully sequenced so that pupils develop a secure understanding of each area. Our curriculum aims to:
Pupils should be taught to use practical scientific methods, processes, and skills and here at Tottenhall, our Science Ninjas scheme supports pupils in carrying out meaningful practical science linked to the National Curriculum. The scheme rewards pupils for demonstrating practical skills during science activities with stickers that showcase one of the four skills: observation, equipment handling, recording, and measuring. The scheme’s principles are as follows:
Alongside the comprehensive curriculum and the Science Ninjas scheme, our pupils receive weekly science lessons, attend science trips, participate in engaging activities during Science Week, and are continually exposed to the benefits of cross-curricular science links to other subjects.

Art and Design
At Tottenhall Infant school we strongly believe that art is a vital part of our curriculum, encouraging creativity, self-expression, and critical thinking. Through studying a diverse range of artists and styles, children develop an understanding of their own and others’ cultural heritage.
We use the national curriculum for Art and Design and ensure that all pupils:
Approach Our pupils explore the visual elements of art including line, tone, texture, colour, pattern, shape, and form. This is achieved successfully through well-planned lessons that build skills and confidence over time.
Teaching and Learning Art is taught weekly each half term, alternating with Design and Technology. In EYFS, children create artwork linked to wider topics, focusing on developing core skills. In Key Stage 1, pupils follow structured units and produce weekly artwork.
Opportunities At Tottenhall Infant school children have the opportunity to participate in an ART DAY where teachers model and demonstrate a piece of art work related to an artist, designer or craftsman to the pupils. This guidance ensures that the pupils create art work influenced by the session taught and the pupils create beautiful work that are visible on displays around the school for all to view. This enables children to build confidence, understanding and develop their skills explored widely as well as interact with their peers where they may work in pairs, or in groups or alone and share their opinions and views on what had been learnt.
They also visit galleries and museums to enrich their understanding and knowledge of the art in the diverse community and their observations made in their surroundings with attention to the environment. Lessons are often inspired by famous artists and linked to subjects such as Science, History, and Geography. Pupils learn new techniques, use key vocabulary, and evaluate their own work and others’ work.
Success Learning is inclusive and differentiated, ensuring all pupils achieve success where the talent of the children’s art work are displayed across the school and celebrated hugely. An art portfolio with each child’s art work are compiled from Nursery all the way to Year 2 which is finally taken home. The pupils make a memorable journey at Tottenhall school with the learning of art and design in an innovative way, inspiring them to go out in the wider world as creative independent imaginative learners.

Computing
Computers play a vital role in the modern world, and many of even the most basic jobs involve technology and computers. We want our pupils to be equipped with using computational thinking and creativity to be able to access, understand and change the world around them.
At Tottenhall Infant School, we recognise that the National Curriculum divides into three strands (computer science, digital literacy and Information technology). The curriculum we use supports children to complete age appropriate computing and prepares them to be safe, active participants in the digital world.
We deliver and teach the computing curriculum through Purple Mash. Purple Mash is an up to date scheme and supports our staff in delivering fun and engaging lessons, which help to raise computing attainment and allows pupils to achieve to their full potential.
Every computing unit in the Purple Mash programme ensures continuity and progression skills, knowledge and understanding across the school. This is done by implementing computing skills in meaningful ways and making appropriate cross curricular skills.
In the Early Years, we aim to provide our pupils with a broad, play-based experience of computing in a range of contexts. We believe in the following:
Every class has an interactive touchscreen board used for whole class teaching. The pupils have access to Laptops and iPads, and use them to make films, write stories, and deepen their computing knowledge.

English
The development of children’s language is crucial to their success across the curriculum. We want pupils to be excellent communicators, to listen actively and to speak with confidence. At Tottenhall Infant School pupils are helped to develop a love of reading and become skilful imaginative writers. Each year group has statutory elements of English which have to be covered. These involve fundamental elements of English such as reading, comprehension, composition, spelling, grammar and punctuation.
Writing
We believe that the learning of writing skills should be embedded across the school. Opportunities for cross curricular links are provided to ensure extended writing is evident across the curriculum. The key skills of writing e.g. spelling, composition are therefore taught explicitly in the context of English lessons, but also indirectly through cross curricular writing tasks in other subjects.
To enable children to develop as effective writers we will teach them to:
Use accurate punctuation and spelling
Our Approach to Reading
Reading is a key and vital skill for our pupils to be able to access the breadth of the curriculum at Tottenhall Infant School. It is a key contributor towards children’s language and communication development as well as improving children’s vocabulary. Reading leads to more highly developed language skills and improves the child’s ability to write well and communicate in a range of contexts and forms.
In addition, reading is a fun and imaginative time for children, which opens doors to all kinds of new worlds for them. The reading curriculum at our school teaches children about the world around them. Through reading a variety of books our children learn about people, places, and events outside of their own experience. As a school we have ensured that we have a range of books and reading materials for children to access and design the curriculum around issues that matter to them such as recycling, friendships, planting and the natural environment.
Being able to read improves children’s concentration, self-esteem and empathy. As children develop, they begin to imagine how they would feel in that situation, place or event.
We understand that reading promotes achievement in all subjects, not just English. Children who are good readers tend to achieve better across the curriculum. We believe this is crucial in improving the life chances of our pupils. The curriculum is adapted to meet the needs of all learners where they are able to make progress and access learning.
All classrooms have inviting reading corners, with fiction and non- fiction books, and dual language texts. Books are sent home frequently. Across the school a reading record book is maintained to encourage a home school partnership. Children have access to a range of appropriate book banded texts to read both at home and school. These books are well matched to children’s phonic knowledge to allow them to make good progress. In order to foster the love of reading we organise termly visits to the local library for children, have a focus author of the month and opportunities for children to listen to adults read. We empower our children by ensuring reading skills and opportunities intersect all areas of the curriculum.
Phonics
At Tottenhall Infant School we use Little Wandle Letters and Sounds Revised. This is a complete systematic synthetic phonics programme (SSP) developed for schools by schools. It is a complete teaching programme meeting all the expectations of the National Curriculum and prepares children to go beyond the expectations of the Phonics Screening Check.
This is a systematic programme for teaching phonic skills for children starting in the nursery, with the aim of them becoming fluent readers by age seven. It is a recognised synthetic phonics scheme where children first learn their letter sounds and names, and then apply these to word building. The children will also learn a variety of other key words by sight.
Reading in class
In reception children have a weekly guided reading session using texts that are clearly matched to their phonic level.
In year KS1 children are taught reading through guided reading sessions using texts that matched to children’s phonic levels and reading fluency. Children are expected to use their skills to discuss books, vocabulary, authors, share opinions and answer a range of verbal and written comprehension questions.
How you can help your child with reading
We always value the support parents give their child at home. Please ensure your child is reading every day and leave a comment in their reading record. You can also visit the local library and remember to attend our reading breakfasts during the year.

Geography
At Tottenhall Infant School, we are fortunate to have a rich local environment and strong community links, which form the heart of our curriculum. Our vision is to help children develop a deep understanding of what makes our world special, preparing them for their future as responsible global citizens.
Our Geography curriculum begins with the children’s own locality and gradually expands to include countries and cultures from around the world. Learning is developed through a curriculum that inspires curiosity and exploration. Children are encouraged to explore their local area, relate it to maps, and understand their place in the country and the wider world. They are also equipped with the skills to use a range of maps and atlases confidently.
We help children explore and master essential geographical skills and knowledge through exciting, cross-curricular lessons. Each term, learning is brought to life around a key topic allowing children to make connections across subjects while discovering the world around them.
Our curriculum is regularly reviewed to ensure progression across the school and to make certain that children are equipped with the knowledge and skills they need to thrive in an ever-changing world.

History
At Tottenhall, we aspire for all children to be happy, curious, and engaged learners who enjoy discovering the past. Our History curriculum provides opportunities for children to build on prior knowledge as they progress through the school, deepening their understanding of people, events, and changes over time.
Each topic encourages pupils to explore history in practical and meaningful ways. Children record and present their learning through a variety of formats such as fact sheets, true/false information cards, and posters. Educational visits and themed days are carefully planned to enrich the curriculum, consolidate learning, and inspire a lifelong interest in History.
Teaching and planning are guided by the aims and core knowledge set out in the National Curriculum. Teachers create exciting and stimulating lessons that develop pupils’ historical knowledge, skills, and understanding. Children are given opportunities to handle and examine artefacts, helping them to make tangible connections with the past.
Our History curriculum includes topics such as changes within living memory, events beyond living memory, the lives of significant individuals, toys past and present, and Kings and Queens. Through these engaging themes, pupils gain a strong foundation for future historical learning.

PSHE (Personal, Social and Health Education)
Our personal, social and health education (PSHE) programme promotes children's personal, social and economic development, as well as their health and wellbeing. It helps to give children the knowledge, skills and understanding they need to lead confident, healthy, independent lives and to become informed, active, responsible citizens.
At Tottenhall, children’s wellbeing, happiness and safety are our first priority, and PSHE is the key vehicle through which we share this with children. We regard PSHE as an important, integral component of the whole curriculum; it is central to our approach and at the core of our ethos.

Physical Education
Physical Education at Tottenhall Infant School is a very important part of our curriculum. All children in Key Stage 1 engage in a minimum of 2 hours each week and this is delivered through a broad and balanced curriculum with activities designed to be enjoyable, vigorous, purposeful and regular. In the Early Years, we encourage physical activity and a love for the outdoors through having outdoor play every day.
At Tottenhall your children are given many opportunities to develop their interests through a planned PE programme that aims to develop knowledge, understanding, skills and above all, positive attitudes towards sport and physical activity. Our curriculum includes games, dance and gymnastics. Individual talents and sporting aptitudes are encouraged, together with those social and personal qualities that come from taking part in both team and individual activities. These include the acceptance of responsibility, loyalty and cooperation, determination, tolerance and the enjoyment of success as well as simply taking part
